title: Defendant Goes Nuts After Courtroom Verdict
description:

transcript.text: In Winnebago County, Wisconsin, after a defendant is denied release from jail by a judge, he becomes infuriated and is about to unleash his rage on the officers escorting him out of court. 76, control elevator, second. Come on, man, we got to get going. I'm not doing this shit. Don't say anything, bitch. Okay, you're proving everybody's point. That's great. I'm not. For months, don't tell you. Don't tell the shit. No, I don't give a fuck. Take a breath for a minute, okay? No, you just shut the door, my mom? You know what, officer? Just relax, no. We're going to lift you up, man, right? All right. Why didn't need my stomach? You're good. You're okay. Hey, you're okay, all right? Oh, I want to be all the shoe me. You want to us on? Who's the one that need me and my... You said you're not feeling well. It's where to get you to the medical attention. What's like you're feeling fine now? Kicking, man. Dude, that's a false shot kicking. After over 20 minutes. of non-stop resisting, officers were finally able to restrain the suspect and transport him to jail. He was charged with two counts of attempting to disarm a peace officer, battery to a law enforcement officer, and discharging bodily fluids. He pleaded no contest to attempting to disarm a peace officer and throwing or discharging a bodily fluid at a public safety worker. The charge of battery or threat to a judge, prosecutor, or law enforcement officer was dismissed. He was sentenced to four years of probation and 229 days in jail for each of his charges. totaling eight years of probation and 458 days in jail. Court records indicate he has since been charged with battery by prisoners on not just one, but two separate incidents. He has also since been charged with threats to cause bodily harm against court staff, resisting obstructing and disorderly conduct on yet another separate incident. For all of those incidents, he is presumed innocent and less proven guilty in a court of law. It's crazy how one outbursts can destroy everything you've been working towards. You sit in front of a judge hoping for a chance, Maybe a little mercy, maybe a glimpse of freedom, and then in one split second, this guy threw his away. See, every inmate dreams that light at the end of the tunnel. The early release and a chance to start over. See, the system, as slow as it is, does reward good behavior. Keep your head down and follow the rules, stay respectful, and suddenly your name lands in front of a parole board that actually wants to help you. When you act like this, you're showing that board exactly why you shouldn't be trusted on the street. So inmates who play a smart know the game isn't about manipulation, it's about discipline. The court doesn't forget and officers don't forget, and even your own public defender might throw his hands up and say you made this impossible. You had a chance to show restraint, and instead you showed the exact behavior that landed you there in the first place. And this man didn't just attack officers. He attacked his own future because every time you act out in the system, you're proving you're not ready for the freedom you're begging for. And the saddest part is, all he had to do was walk away.
